record.paper_title: Theoretical descriptions of compound-nuclear reactions: open problems & challenges
record.original_question: How can the compound-nucleus formation process in a surrogate reaction be modeled accurately enough that cross sections extracted indirectly from surrogate measurements are reliable?

evidence.quote: The accuracy of the extracted cross section depends on how well the compound-nucleus formation process in the surrogate reaction is described.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an indirect measurement scheme (a "surrogate" reaction) used to determine a desired compound-nucleus reaction cross section σ_CN(a,b)(E) = σ_CN^a(E) · P_CN(b,E), where:

- σ_CN^a(E) denotes the formation cross section of a compound nucleus in a desired entrance channel a at center-of-mass energy E,
- P_CN(b,E) denotes the branching (decay) probability of that compound nucleus into an exit channel b, with ∑_b P_CN(b,E) = 1,
- The desired entrance channel a is experimentally inaccessible.

In the surrogate approach, one instead populates the same compound nucleus through a different (accessible) reaction d + D → c + B*, where B* denotes the equilibrated compound nucleus, and one measures coincidence probabilities

P_δb(E) = ∫ F_δ(E, J, π) · G_CN(b; E, J, π) dJ dπ,

where F_δ(E, J, π) is the spin–parity (J,π) population distribution of B* produced in the surrogate reaction at excitation energy E, and G_CN(b; E, J, π) is the conditional decay probability of B* into channel b. The desired branching is

P_CN(b,E) = ∫ F_a(E, J, π) · G_CN(b; E, J, π) dJ dπ,

with F_a the (J,π) distribution that would be produced via the desired entrance channel a.

Problem. Develop a quantitative theoretical model of the compound-nucleus formation step in the surrogate reaction—i.e., a calculation of F_δ(E, J, π) including direct, pre-equilibrium, and equilibration dynamics—accurate enough that, when combined with a model of G_CN(b; E, J, π) and standard optical-model estimates of σ_CN^a(E), the indirectly extracted cross section σ_CN(a,b)(E) agrees with direct measurements (where available) to within a prescribed tolerance over the relevant range of E, for nuclei in the actinide and rare-earth regions. Equivalently: provide a controlled procedure for computing F_δ(E, J, π) for surrogate reactions of types (d,p), (d,pf), (³He,α), and (α,α′) such that the systematic error introduced by the surrogate approximation in the extracted σ_CN(a,b)(E) is bounded.
artifact.status_search_result: Modeling of compound-nucleus formation in surrogate reactions remains an active research challenge. Recent work (e.g., Escher et al., Phys. Rev. C / Phys. Rev. Lett. 2018–2024) has produced improved spin-parity distribution calculations for (d,p) and (d,pf) surrogates and benchmarking against direct measurements, but a fully predictive, generally accurate description of the surrogate formation step (especially treating direct/pre-equilibrium/equilibration consistently) is not yet established. The problem is widely regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Theoretical descriptions of compound-nuclear reactions
status_evidence.snippet: The accuracy of the extracted cross section depends on how well the compound-nucleus formation process in the surrogate reaction is described.
status_evidence.claim: Surrogate CN-formation modeling identified as an outstanding challenge.

status_evidence.title: Constraining Neutron Capture Cross Sections for Unstable Nuclei with Surrogate Reaction Data and Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Escher et al. demonstrate progress combining surrogate (d,p) measurements with reaction theory to extract (n,γ) cross sections, while noting remaining theoretical uncertainties in the formation step.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress but full accurate modeling remains open.
